title: Adjust a drum brake
summary: Set the lever or pedal free play on a cable or rod drum brake so it bites early and doesn't drag.

steps.text: Put the bike on the center stand so the wheel spins freely.
Measure how far the lever end or pedal moves before the brake starts to bite. Most bikes call for 10 to 20 mm; check your manual.
Turn the adjusting nut at the brake arm on the wheel. Tighten it to reduce free play, loosen it to add free play.
Spin the wheel. It should turn without rubbing when the brake is released.
steps.caution: If the wheel drags or warms up after a ride, back the adjuster off. A dragging brake overheats and fades.

steps.text: Make sure the nut's cutout sits fully on the brake arm pin, then check that the brake light comes on when the brake is applied.
If the wear indicator arrow reaches the end of its range, the shoes need replacing instead of adjusting.
